Going Dairy-Free? 5 Reasons Your Protein Shake Should Switch to Beef and Egg

By the PaleoPro TeamUpdated September 2026

Summary: Whey is made from milk, so when dairy goes, the shake usually goes with it. The common replacement is plant protein, and the common cost is fewer grams per scoop and a thinner amino acid profile. Paleo Protein takes the other route: grass-fed beef protein isolate and egg white, 26g of complete protein per scoop, and no milk ingredients at all. Your shake can come with you.

Dairy-Free by Design

1. Whey and casein are milk, and “lactose-free” whey is still dairy

Both whey and casein are separated out of milk. Taking the lactose out of whey leaves you with a dairy protein, and for some people the protein itself is the trouble. Paleo Protein starts somewhere else: grass-fed beef protein isolate and egg white. There’s no milk ingredient in the formula, so there’s no whey, casein or lactose to remove.

26g Per Scoop

2. 26 of the 30 grams in every scoop are protein

That leaves about 120 calories, 0 to 1 gram of carbs and zero sugar. Many plant-based powders land between 15 and 20 grams a scoop, which is why going dairy-free so often means giving up protein. Typical whey gives you 20 to 25.

3. It has all nine essential amino acids

Beef isolate and egg white together deliver every essential amino acid, leucine included. Single-source plant proteins often run low in at least one, which is why so many of them are sold as blends.

See the complete protein
Tested Against Whey

4. In an 8-week training study, beef protein kept pace with whey

People in a resistance training program took beef protein isolate, chicken protein or whey after workouts for eight weeks. All three groups gained lean mass, with no significant difference between the proteins (Sharp et al., Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research, 2018). It tested the ingredient, not our finished powder, but it answers the question whey drinkers ask first: will I lose ground if I switch?

Plain Naked is beef protein isolate, egg white protein and sunflower lecithin. Aztec Vanilla and Mayan Mocha add natural flavors and monk fruit; Ancient Cacao adds cocoa. No gums, fillers, artificial sweeteners or stevia. A typical tub of whey lists 15 to 25.

The Switch, Explained

Whey is a milk protein. Grass-fed beef protein isolate and egg white give you a complete protein with all nine essential amino acids and no milk ingredients, so a dairy-free diet keeps its shake.

Not at all. The protein is flavor-neutral, then blended into Aztec Vanilla, Ancient Cacao, Mayan Mocha, or left Plain Naked. It mixes in 12 to 16 oz of water and drinks lighter than a thick whey shake.

There are no milk ingredients, no soy and no gums in the formula, which are the usual suspects. Digestion is individual, so we can’t promise how yours will react. That is what the 60 days are for.

Yes. No grains, dairy, legumes or added sugar. Plain Naked is only the two proteins and sunflower lecithin, so it fits a strict Whole30. It does contain egg, so it isn’t AIP-compliant.
